en: Year of the Monkey; person born in a Monkey year

examples.en: They say I'm curious because I'm a Monkey in the zodiac.
My older sister is a Monkey and I am a Dog.
I met a friend who was born in a Monkey year.
Are you a Monkey too, teacher? That's the same as me.

examples.ko: 원숭이띠 해는 열두 해마다 다시 돌아와요.
examples.en: A Monkey year comes around again every twelve years.

examples.ko: 올해 원숭이띠가 운이 좋다고 해서 기대돼요.
examples.en: They say Monkeys have good luck this year, so I'm looking forward to it.

explain: 십이지 동물로 태어난 해를 말해요. '무슨 띠예요?'에 '원숭이띠예요'라고 대답해요. '신년 운세'에서 띠별로 운을 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: 2016 was the Year of the Monkey.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 원숭이에 해당하는 해를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the year itself, not the person born in it.

phrases.en: I read the Monkey sign's fortune in the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띠별 운세를 읽을 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when reading zodiac fortunes.

phrases.en: I'm a Monkey. My friend is an Ox.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest answer to 무슨 띠예요?

explain_en: It names the zodiac animal of the year you were born. You answer '무슨 띠예요?' with '원숭이띠예요'. Zodiac signs are often used in New Year fortune readings.

examples.en: Tomorrow is my grandfather's memorial day, so I'm going to my uncle's house.
On memorial day the family gathers to prepare food.

examples.ko: 제삿날이 다가오면 어머니가 장을 많이 보세요.
examples.en: When the memorial day approaches, my mother does a lot of grocery shopping.
It's a relief that this year's memorial day falls on the weekend.

examples.ko: 제삿날 아침부터 집에서 전 부치는 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: From the morning of the memorial day, the house smelled of pan-fried jeon.
I told the office it was a memorial day and left early.

explain: '제사'는 지내는 일이고 '제삿날'은 그 날짜예요. 같은 날을 '기일'이라고도 하는데, 일상 대화에서는 '제삿날이 다음 주예요'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Next week is my grandmother's memorial day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제삿날'과 같은 날인데, 조금 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the same day, but a slightly more formal word.

phrases.example: 제삿날에는 온 가족이 모여 제사를 지내요.
phrases.en: On the memorial day, the whole family gathers and holds the ritual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제사를 하는 일을 말할 때 '지내다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '지내다' is the verb used for holding the ritual.

phrases.en: The memorial day was coming up, so my mother went grocery shopping.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the date is getting close.

explain_en: '제사' is the ritual itself and '제삿날' is the date it is held. The same day is also called '기일', but in everyday talk people often say things like '제삿날이 다음 주예요'.

examples.ko: 투표일이 공휴일이라서 여행 가는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Voting day is a holiday, so some people go on trips.

examples.ko: 투표일 전에 후보들의 공약을 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: Before voting day, I checked the candidates' pledges.
When is voting day for this election?

examples.ko: 투표일에 일이 있으면 미리 사전 투표를 하세요.
examples.en: If you have something on voting day, vote early in advance.
There aren't many days left until voting day.
I marked voting day on the calendar so I wouldn't forget.

explain: '선거일'과 거의 같은 날을 가리키지만, '사전 투표일'처럼 미리 투표하는 날을 따로 말할 때도 써요. '투표일'은 투표하는 날, '선거일'은 선거가 있는 날이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: On voting day I went to the polling place with my family.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '에' says when the voting day is.

phrases.example: 사전 투표일은 선거 날보다 며칠 먼저예요.
phrases.en: Early voting day is a few days before election day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 투표하는 날을 따로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer separately to the days for early voting.

phrases.en: On election day, many schools are closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투표일과 거의 같은 날이지만 선거가 있는 날이라는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usually the same day, but it feels like 'the day of the election.'

explain_en: It points to nearly the same day as '선거일', but it is also used for separate voting days such as '사전 투표일' (early voting day). '투표일' feels like the day you vote, and '선거일' like the day the election takes place.

examples.en: I memorize Korean words whenever I have a spare moment.
I know you're busy, but come visit when you get a chance.

examples.ko: 요즘은 틈날 때마다 공원에서 산책을 해요.
examples.en: These days I take a walk in the park whenever I have time.
I found a free moment at lunchtime and took a short nap.
Rest even briefly when you get a free moment.
After the meeting ends, I'll call you as soon as I get a free moment.

explain: '시간이 나다'와 비슷하지만, 바쁜 중에 잠깐 생긴 짧은 시간이라는 느낌이 강해요. '틈나는 대로', '틈날 때마다'처럼 자주 쓰고, '틈이 나다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I read books whenever I have a spare moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 생길 때마다 바로 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means doing something as soon as you get free time.

phrases.en: I call my parents whenever I have a free moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '틈나는 대로'와 비슷하고 반복해서 한다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 틈나는 대로, with a feeling of doing it again and again.
phrases.en_equiv: every time I get a chance

phrases.en: If I find some time today, I plan to take a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '틈나다'와 같은 뜻이고, '이'를 넣어 말할 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 틈나다, with '이' added.

explain_en: It is similar to '시간이 나다' but strongly suggests a short gap in an otherwise busy schedule. It is common in '틈나는 대로' and '틈날 때마다', and you can also say '틈이 나다'.
